newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Perm Motors says 29 bln rbls loss in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Russian Perm Motors says 29 bln rbls loss in 1996.

text.p: NOTES: These figures are prepared to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis. Russian accounts are designed to meet the requirements of the tax authorities. Russian companies can choose whether to show revenues and spending on a cash or accruals basis. Definitions of profit and assets differ significantly from those in the West, and converting Russian accounts to international standards can turn a profit into a loss.
Figures are not adjusted for inflation or the depreciation of the rouble, but the following data may be helpful.
Dollar on Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX):
Year-on-year consumer price inflation rate in December 1996 was 21.8 percent in December 1996 after 131 percent in December 1995 and 215 percent in December 1994 and 840 percent in December 1993.
AO Permskiye Motory shareholders did not confirm the balance sheet or profit and loss figures at the annual general meeting held on Saturday.
The Board of Directors, elected at the meeting on Saturday, fired chief executive Vladimir Kinderknekht, a spokesman for Interros-Prom, a major shareholder, told Reuters.
The spokesman said Vadim Isachenko, former plant employee and a Russian Federation Security Council aide, had been appointed acting chief executive.

Valentin Stepankov, former Russian prosecutor-general and currently Duma deputy from Perm region, was elected chairman of the board, replacing Mikail Kuzmenko, chief executive of company AO Aviadvigatel.
Five representatives from Interros-Prom, which owns 17.7 percent of Perm Motors' shares, were elected to the board of directors on Saturday. There are 15 members of the board in total.

Perm employees own 18.8 percent of shares, the government holds 14.3 percent and AO Monetarnaya Finansovaya Kompaniya owns 10.1 percent. Natural gas producer and transporter Gazprom owns a 2.9 percent stake. Company makes aviation engines and turbines.
